items.weakness_text: The experiments are narrow: only one domain and one benchmark family. Claims about general planning improvement are therefore not well supported.
items.ac_evidence: Experimental scope stays narrow despite budget explanations.

items.weakness_text: There are no comparisons with so many other structured prompting methods (eg CoS, ReAct, least-to-most, chain-of-thought scaffolding and so on). It is unclear whether TMK offers advantages beyond simply using more structured json templates.
items.ac_evidence: Citing literature that CoT doesn't help planning doesn't substitute for direct comparisons with alternative prompting methods.

items.weakness_text: The explanation of why TMK helps remains speculative. No ablation isolates whether improvements come from the educational knowledge model framing or just from better formatting and key-word cues.
items.ac_evidence: No ablations isolate whether gains come from TMK's structure versus simply providing more organized JSON formatting.

items.weakness_text: The reviewer finds it difficult to understand what is the core idea/contribution of TMK prompting method proposed in the paper. The paper did poorly in explaining the proposed prompting method.
The paper proposes a prompting method, yet there are no examples of the prompt in the paper.
items.ac_evidence: included prompt examples in the Appendix

items.weakness_text: Experimental evidence of the advantage of the proposed method is very limited: only OpenAI models, only one task (blocksworld), and many numbers are missing (Table 2)

Many fields are missing in Table 2, especially Plain Text + One Shot. Note that it's unfair to compare the other two columns (TMK + One Shot vs Plain Text + Zero Shot). The paper does not have other main results.
items.ac_evidence: The one-shot TMK vs zero-shot baseline comparison remains potentially unfair.

items.weakness_text: It does not make sense to replace standard description of blockworlds into irrelevant mystery or random words. No LLM learns it during pre-training, nor people will use those words to describe tasks, nor they will use LLMs like this.
It's not easy to understand what TMK is doing (lacking a concrete example of the prompt/formatting).
items.ac_evidence: included prompt examples in the Appendix

items.weakness_text: The method is only experimented on blockworlds, which is a toy dataset easily solvable by non-machine learning algorithms like DFS. It's unknown whether the method can be generalized to other meaningful domains, such as mathematical, logical, legal reasonings.
items.ac_evidence: Experimental scope stays narrow despite budget explanations.
